notes: Tinned vegetable ghee (Al-Ghazal etc.) is the everyday frying/cooking fat in Palestinian markets; solid at 20C, no fridge needed.
Clarified butter; sold loose by the waqiya (250 g) in Palestinian spice shops and tinned (e.g. Dutch cow ghee). Keeps months unrefrigerated if kept clean.
Softens and goes rancid faster than ghee without refrigeration; buy small packs.

Sesame halva; a staple cheap breakfast/snack and part of UNRWA/WFP parcels (https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom/features/supporting-most-vulnerable-gaza-vital-food). Stable at room temperature; oil separates in heat.
Sealed jars are shelf-stable; apricot jam jars appeared in GHF aid boxes (2025). Once opened keeps a few weeks unrefrigerated.
Effectively non-perishable; sold by the waqiya (250 g) or in jars.
Eaten with tahini (dibs w tahini) at breakfast.
Hebron speciality; also Turkish imports (pekmez).
Souring agent used in Gazan cooking (with sumac and lemon).
Nutella reported back on Gaza supermarket shelves (NPR, Jan 2026). Oil may separate above 30C.
Not a traditional staple; imported (US, Lotus, Israeli).
Sealed bottles shelf-stable; opened keeps ~1 month unrefrigerated if kept cool.
Sealed jars are stable; once opened it needs refrigeration (spoils in 1-2 days at 25C+). Prefer small packs or sachets.
Vinegar-based bottled chili sauce.
Gazan shatta: ground red chillies with salt, lemon/oil; also made at home. Jarred versions in 370-560 g jars.
Minor item.
Used for pickling (makdous, lift) and salads; روح الخل (acetic essence) is diluted at home.
Called 'Maggi' generically; sold singly or in boxes of 8-24 cubes (about 10 g each; Knorr Egypt 9 g each).
Central to Gaza cooking (sumaghiyya, fattoush, musakhan).

name_en: Gaza dukkah (toasted wheat, dill seed and chili blend)
notes: Gaza's everyday bread-dip blend (eaten with olive oil); The Gaza Kitchen describes it with dill seed and chili. Toasted wheat can go stale/rancid faster than pure spices.
Characteristic Gaza spice (dagga, dukkah, fish). Gazans call fresh dill jarada.
Mostly for coffee; sold in 65 g (quarter waqiya) steps because it is expensive.
Tea and ka'ak/ma'amoul.
Cheap lemon substitute when lemons are scarce.
In Palestine plain 'bhar' usually means allspice.
Used in meghli (caraway rice pudding) for births.
Called qizha; also ground into qizha paste.
Gaza is a fishing city; blends usually contain cumin, coriander, dill seed and chili.
